item.text: I’ll record your approval of the job-card direction and give you the complete plan in one place, including every scroll beat, interaction and fallback. This remains planning only.

# Planning handover

## Request

Plan a distinctive personal portfolio for Mina Park, with relevant 3D and scroll-driven motion. The eventual plan must cover concept, full scroll sequence, section content, colours, typography, phone behaviour and supporting site requirements. Do not build anything.

## Completed

- Read all three supplied files: `material/cv.md`, `material/blog.md`, `material/message.md`.
- Read the storyfolio skill and its profile-reading reference.
- Created a sourced fact sheet, uncertainty list and decision record.

## Current stop

Stop 3: storyboard review. Mina answered the key factual questions and authorized judgment on uncovered matters. Answers are recorded in `facts.md`; unconfirmed facts remain explicitly marked. Three concepts exist in `concepts.md`; the designer chose the job card under that authorization. Full plan exists in `storyboard.md`. Mina has not yet approved the storyboard. No website code has been created.

## Next

Obtain a yes to the storyboard or incorporate requested changes. Do not ask Mina to choose the concept again: she already authorized the designer to decide. On storyboard approval update this handover to record it and state that building is outside this planning-only skill version. Final captions are a later task; no captions or implementation should be invented now.

## Planning files

- `facts.md`: original sources, Mina's corrections, answer status and factual dependencies.
- `concepts.md`: three distinct form/object concepts and authorized selection.
- `storyboard.md`: chapters, beats, scroll distances, content sources, palette/type, phone/fallbacks, supporting requirements and future verification.
- `decided-for-you.md`: choices, reasoning and how to change them.

## Outstanding publication dependencies

Public contact/blog destinations; current student/placement dates; selected-asset authorship and permissions; bracket baseline and collaborator credits. These do not prevent planning review and must not be guessed. No team placing, guessed bike count or testimonials in the planned portfolio.
# Mina Park — job-card storyboard

Status: complete planning proposal; storyboard approval pending. No website built. Final captions are not written at this stage. Working headings and factual content specifications below are not final marketing copy.

## Waiting on Mina

1. Current student year, placement availability and public email. The supplied second-year description is provisional; no availability year is assumed.
2. A real Slow Miles URL. Keep the blog separate; no example-domain links in a published site.
3. Authorship/public-use permission for selected bike photos and team CAD, and confirmation of anyone identifiable in them. No actual assets were supplied. Planned image slots are conditional; unapproved assets do not appear.
4. Bracket baseline and collaborator credits before detailed comparison captions. Do not imply sole authorship, physical testing or validated structural performance.

These are future publication dependencies. They do not prevent reviewing this plan. Unanswered learning questions, repair counts, job-title questions and detailed charger test conditions are handled by omission or qualification, not assumptions.

## Idea

Question: **How do you know a part is ready to work?**

Form: Mina's job card, using the five fields in the order she described. The page exposes the difference between finding a fault, designing a change and checking a result. The end answers the question by distinguishing her reported physical prototype observation from a bracket still awaiting manufacture. It never states that her CAD bracket is ready for service.

One continuous object: **six newly designed portfolio job-card leaves**, two for each of the bike, bracket and charger. Their faces hold work images if cleared, otherwise ordinary records of the confirmed facts. They remain recognisable together as a shallow paper stack. They are not fictional customer job cards and do not contain customer names, manufactured service histories or signatures.

The cards serve as the evidence layout, not a background sculpture. Separating them communicates symptom versus finding; pairing them communicates project versus contribution; their final status arrangement communicates what is and is not checked. Every relation also has an HTML equivalent.

## Card contents

| Leaf | Face content | Fallback if asset unavailable |
|---|---|---|
| Bike A | Conditional garage-floor parts photograph from the documented inventory | Text record of the inventory and keep/fix/replace labels, linked to writing only when URL is real |
| Bike B | Conditional photograph identifying the cracked hub flange, if the supplied image supports that identification | Confirmed blog title/summary and distinction between reported wheel symptom and hub finding |
| Bracket A | Conditional cleared CAD view of the redesigned mounting bracket | Record of redesign involvement and CAD/simulation weight reduction |
| Bracket B | Conditional cleared comparison view with a confirmed baseline | Status record: not manufactured or physically tested; planned November machining shown as a dated plan only if still current |
| Charger A | Conditional prototype or gear-train/housing photograph if Mina later supplies one | Text attribution: four-person module project; Mina's gear train and housing |
| Charger B | Confirmed report of prototype behaviour | Same report; no invented chart, efficiency rating or battery test data |

Do not invent visual geometry of the bracket or charger from their names. The 3D object is paper, so it can be planned without pretending that a product model was supplied.

## Chapters

| Chapter | Its name in the form | Role | What it tells | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reported fault | Opening; who | Mina's identity, work scope, guiding question and immediate project proof | Bike inventory leaf leads; six leaves gather into a shallow stack | Three project jump links, contact shortcut, skip link |
| 2 | Findings | Where from; how | The rear-wheel finding; her actual job-card and logbook process; concise experience dates | Two bike leaves separate as symptom/finding; other leaves stay visible behind | Writing link if real; open static evidence detail |
| 3 | Parts | What | All three projects, scope and status | Six leaves fan into three two-leaf exhibits | Accessible project links and image enlargement where available |
| 4 | Work carried out | Individual contribution | Bracket redesign; charger gear train and housing; restoration documented in writing | Three pairs align with their HTML contribution records | Inline detail disclosure for each project |
| 5 | Test ride | Outcomes; close | Bike test ride as her process, charger's poor physical result, bracket awaiting physical tests; contact | Three pairs line up with explicit text statuses, then restack | Contact, CV, project links; back to top |

The chapter heading Test ride is Mina's job-card field. Its content explicitly distinguishes a co-op test ride from a charger prototype observation and bracket validation. Do not suggest a specific restored-bike test ride occurred.

## Beats

Screen counts are approximate desktop scroll distances, not animation waits. Total target: approximately 6.5 viewport heights, readable in two minutes. On short screens the text determines height. No scroll snapping, compulsory dwell or long empty transitions.

### 1 — Reported fault

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | On their faces | Chapter adds | Caption basis, not final caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1A | 1 | Bike A face up; five leaves offset behind; small gather motion on first scroll | Inventory photograph if cleared; otherwise inventory record. Small previews of bracket status and charger contribution | HTML name, provisional student description, question, project/contact shortcuts and one factual proof preview | Identity: CV opening. Inventory: blog entry 2 and answer Q6. Proof: bracket 18% CAD/simulation reduction, explicitly unbuilt and untested, from Q2 |

The opening is usable before motion or scene load. No full-screen loader or autoplay intro. It does not depend on a learning story Mina has not supplied.

### 2 — Findings

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | On their faces | Chapter adds | Caption basis, not final caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2A | 0.75 | Bike pair side by side; other leaves in rear stack | Reported rear-wheel symptom and cracked hub-flange finding; image only if it actually depicts the finding | Two text labels and a short evidence source link | Wheel finding: blog entry 4. Do not claim a completed successful repair |
| 2B | 0.75 | Same bike pair aligns with the five-field job-card sequence; other cards shift minimally | Confirmed inventory/finding faces retained | HTML sequence of Mina's five fields; workshop logbook reference; small dated context strip | Process: answer Q7. Context: co-op 2023–present from CV; Hallam Racing October 2025–present confirmed Q3. Dates are source-stated and must be reviewed before publication |

No co-op customer records, fictional fault entries or manufactured workshop anecdotes. No separate inflated biography section.

### 3 — Parts

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | On their faces | Chapter adds | Caption basis, not final caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3A | 1.25 | All six leaves spread into three readable pairs; faces remain near front-on | Bike inventory/finding; bracket CAD/status; charger contribution/result | Three HTML project summaries with status labels and links to inline details | All work: facts.md project records, blog entries 2/4 and answers Q2/Q4. No ranking or repair count |

Images never rotate away while their corresponding text is being read. Card selection uses an ordinary link or button; dragging and hover are optional, never necessary.

### 4 — Work carried out

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | On their faces | Chapter adds | Caption basis, not final caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4A | 1.25 | Same three pairs become a vertical arrangement beside contribution records; selected pair moves forward slightly | Existing evidence faces; no new decorative object | Bracket redesign scope; charger gear train/housing and group of four; restoration writing; compact skills line | Attribution: CV bracket statement, Q2 limits and Q4 charger contribution. Skills: SolidWorks, MATLAB, some Python; lathe/mill induction only. Do not infer tools used for a specific project |

This stage adds what Mina did rather than repeating gallery thumbnails. Bracket collaborators remain a clearly marked planning dependency. Charger details specify an observed limitation, not an invented cause or lesson.

### 5 — Test ride

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | On their faces | Chapter adds | Caption basis, not final caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5A | 0.75 | Three pairs in a status row; no colour-only grading or progress percentages | Bike process record; charger observation; bracket untested status | Text distinctions: check used in her bike-work process; prototype worked poorly; CAD/simulation only, awaiting manufacture | Q7 process; Q4 four minutes for one percentage point as Mina's report with conditions unspecified; Q2 18% CAD/simulation reduction and not physically tested |
| 5B | 0.75 | Same six leaves restack; evidence remains accessible through links | Top leaf shows portfolio summary/contact designation; underlying work faces unchanged | Closing answer specification: distinguish evidence from readiness; placement contact and CV; blog link if real | Closing reasoning comes from Q2/Q4/Q7, not an attributed personal philosophy quote. Contact goal chosen for confirmed placement-application audience |

No fabricated successful bike restoration outcome, no competition result, no guessed bike count and no testimonials.

## Thirty-second and two-minute paths

- First screen: Mina's name, provisional second-year mechanical-engineering description, three work links, a qualified bracket proof preview and contact shortcut. A recruiter need not scroll to identify the work or reach her.
- Persistent small rail: Reported fault / Findings / Parts / Work carried out / Test ride; plain-text compact version on phones. Direct project anchors bypass the animation sequence.
- 'Skip to contact' and 'Skip to content' are keyboard accessible. Addressable anchors support sharing and browser back/forward. Direct anchor entry renders the correct settled scene without replaying previous chapters.
- The full read takes approximately two minutes. Additional project detail uses native inline disclosures and optional images, so the main narrative stays short.

## Without the scene

All identity, evidence, attribution, statuses and contact are ordinary HTML. Canvas has no unique text or only copy of essential content. The semantic reading order matches the five job-card fields. Scene is supplementary and hidden from assistive technology; equivalent diagrams/images have useful alt text.

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | Single-column HTML with the same five chapters. Static pairs of evidence cards in normal flow by default; no pinned full-height canvas. Name, one proof and project/contact links precede the first large image. Comfortable 16–18px text, at least 44px controls, no horizontal scroll. No information on hover. A wider capable phone may receive a small optional scene only after content loads; no device-orientation control |
| With reduced motion | No card translation, rotation, parallax, smooth scrolling or pinned scene. Static settled card pairs at each chapter. Anchor jumps use ordinary instant navigation |
| With no WebGL | Static HTML cards and approved images, including side-by-side symptom/finding and explicit project status labels. No error banner obscuring the page |
| With no JavaScript | Complete five-chapter HTML, standard anchor navigation, native details disclosures, image links, CV download and contact link. The canvas is absent; content and layout remain usable |

## Look and type

Choose A below under Mina's authorization. The other two are full material directions for future comparison; do not build previews now.

| Look | Ground | Ink | One accent | Piece surface |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A — Workshop paper, chosen | Warm off-white #F3EFE6 | Charcoal #242824 | Deep workshop green #285745 | Uncoated light paper #FFFCF4, fine printed rules, restrained edge shadows |
| B — Clean drawing sheet | Cool off-white #EDF1F2 | Graphite #202A31 | Technical blue #2455A4 | Smooth white card, precise fine rules, minimal shadow |
| C — Night workbench | Near-black #1E2422 | Warm paper #F4F0E5 | Muted brass #CFB473 | Dark-backed cream cards, clear ink, subdued side lighting |

Reason for A: the material is a paper record used in hands-on work; the warm surface makes actual parts/CAD images the focus. This is a design choice, not a claim about the colour of Mina's workshop or preferences. Green is an accent, not a universal 'passed' badge. Labels always carry status in words. Verify all actual text/focus/border contrast during a future build; target WCAG AA.

- **Text:** self-hosted Source Sans 3, regular and semibold. Clear paragraphs, compact headings and numerals. Use a system sans fallback.
- **On the leaves and record labels:** self-hosted IBM Plex Mono, regular and medium. It suggests printed record fields without imitating Mina's handwriting. Essential labels also exist in HTML.
- Use editorial scale, not enormous empty hero type: approximately 48–72px desktop name and 34–44px phone name, responsive to available width; body 18px desktop and 16–18px phone; line length around 60–70 characters.
- Avoid grunge overlays, decorative grease stains, fake measurements, noisy cursors and continuous object spinning. The light paper and restrained perspective make evidence readable.

## Motion and future implementation

- Desktop scene: six simple thin rectangular meshes, one camera and restrained lighting. Single object persists throughout; no physics engine or product-model reconstruction required.
- Scroll maps continuously to settled arrangements; card travel happens between reading positions. Cards rest while their evidence is read. Camera changes are small; no fly-through or forced perspective disorientation.
- Native document scroll remains in control. No scroll hijacking, compulsory intro, autoplay sound or forced carousel.
- Suggested future implementation: statically rendered HTML with a small Three.js module for the optional scene; standard CSS for document layout. Add scroll progress only after the accessible baseline works. Framework choice remains open to the host repository.
- Load HTML and opening proof before 3D. Lazy-load the scene, cap render resolution, pause when offscreen or tab is hidden, use compressed responsive images and avoid loading unseen full-size textures. Fall back on context loss or poor frame performance without losing the current chapter.
- Future acceptance targets, not measured results: LCP at most 2.5s, CLS at most 0.1, INP at most 200ms under representative mobile testing. Core content must remain functional if the scene never loads.

## Everything else the site needs

'Build' means include in a future implementation after storyboard approval; nothing is being built in this planning task.

| Requirement | Build, later or never | Who decided and scope |
|---|---|---|
| Way round the page | Build | Designer under Mina's authorization: semantic anchors, project shortcuts, contact skip, keyboard focus and compact phone navigation |
| Page for each project | Later | Designer: start with substantive inline project details; add individual case-study pages when cleared assets and fuller evidence justify them |
| Every project listed | Build | Designer: include bike restoration, bracket and charger. Co-op and Hallam context live in Findings; no CV-only team placing |
| Reach Mina and obtain a CV | Build | Designer: public email link and downloadable accessible PDF once supplied. CV must remove or clearly attribute the team placing, remove guessed counts, qualify bracket result and update dates. No contact form initially |
| What others say | Never for this version | Mina explicitly says no testimonials; no invented quotes |
| Languages | Build: English; later: others | Designer: English supplied, no unconfirmed language claims |
| Shared link and site icon | Build | Designer: factual title/description, canonical URL, social preview of the job-card layout using cleared evidence or type only; simple card-outline favicon. No award/achievement claims |
| Missing address page | Build | Designer: useful 404 with home, project and contact links |
| Blog | Build: external link; later: import | Designer: retain Slow Miles separately; show supplied titles only as titles, not fabricated full posts; link once a real URL exists |
| Chat | Never for this version | Designer: adds little to a two-minute placement review and would introduce unnecessary infrastructure |
| Legal notice where required | Later, before publication | Designer: determine actual hosting jurisdiction, applicable legal requirements and public contact. Sheffield study location does not establish residence or jurisdiction. No guessed legal identity/address |
| Privacy and analytics | Build: minimal baseline; later: analytics | Designer: no trackers or cookies planned. Before launch document actual hosting/service data handling and provide any necessary privacy notice; optional analytics only if a real need arises |
| Accessibility | Build | Designer: semantic headings, keyboard operation, visible focus, alt text, AA contrast, zoom/reflow, reduced-motion support and static fallback |
| Hosting/domain | Later | Designer: choose deployment only in a separately authorized build/publication task; no paid service selected now |
| Maintenance | Build: editable records | Designer: store project contribution/status separately from layout; date future manufacturing statements; update bracket status only from confirmed evidence. Do not silently turn planned November machining into completed work |

## Future review checklist

- Check first-screen identification, evidence and contact without scrolling or waiting for JavaScript.
- Check a complete two-minute path and direct project/contact anchors.
- Check phone reflow, keyboard, screen-reader order, zoom and reduced motion; compare all fallback content against scene content.
- Confirm every project caption's source and scope, image rights, actual contact links, CV dates and collaborator credits.
- Check performance targets on representative phones. Scene quality may reduce before evidence readability does.

## Approval requested

Mina may approve this storyboard or name changes to concept, look or sequence. Final website prose and any implementation are later work. This version of storyfolio plans only; no building follows automatically from approval.

item.text:
The direction is **the job card**: one continuous scroll following the five fields you actually use at the co-op.

The guiding question is **“How do you know a part is ready to work?”** The page answers through your projects: finding a hidden fault, designing a bracket that still needs physical testing, and making a charger whose performance exposed its limitations.

The complete plan is saved in [storyboard.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-student-with-u3DsbZ/docs/story/storyboard.md). No website has been built.

**Details still needed before publication**

1. Your current student year, placement availability and public contact address.
2. The real Slow Miles URL.
3. Authorship and permission for the photographs and team CAD selected for display.
4. The bracket’s comparison baseline and collaborator credits.

These remain unresolved facts. The plan below works around them without guessing.

**The object that carries the story**

Six thin paper cards stay present throughout the desktop scroll. They are designed portfolio records, with two cards for each project:

| Card | What its face holds |
|---|---|
| Bike: inventory | Your garage-floor parts photograph, if cleared; otherwise a record of the documented keep/fix/replace inventory |
| Bike: finding | The cracked hub-flange finding, with a suitable photograph if available |
| Bracket: design | A cleared CAD view and your redesign contribution |
| Bracket: status | The qualified weight reduction and manufacturing/testing status |
| Charger: contribution | Your gear train and housing within the four-person project |
| Charger: result | Your reported prototype performance |

The 3D object is the paper record itself. We don’t need to invent accurate product geometry or turn a generic gear into your emblem.

The cards’ arrangements explain relationships: symptom beside finding, project beside contribution, result beside validation status. The same relationships appear in ordinary page content.

**Every part of the page, in order**

The desktop story spans roughly **six to seven screen heights**, including its transitions. That is a layout target for a two-minute visit, without compulsory animation waits.

**1. Reported fault — the opening**

Approximately one screen.

The first view shows:

- Mina Park.
- Your supplied second-year mechanical-engineering description, subject to updating.
- The guiding question.
- Direct links to the bike, bracket and charger.
- A contact shortcut.
- One immediate proof point: the bracket’s reported 18% reduction, clearly qualified as CAD/simulation evidence and physically untested.

The bike inventory card sits face-up, with the other five slightly offset behind it. If its photograph is cleared, the opening visibly begins with your own parts laid out on the garage floor. On the first scroll, the six cards gather into a shallow stack.

Your identity and links are readable immediately. There is no loading screen or introductory sequence to wait through.

**Visitor can click:** each project shortcut, contact, and the keyboard-accessible skip-to-content link.

**2. Findings — what you discover and how you work**

Approximately one and a half screens, in two beats.

First, the bike cards separate into a side-by-side relationship: the rear-wheel symptom and the cracked hub-flange finding. The other four cards remain visible behind them.

This uses the supplied blog summary. It does not claim that the repair was completed successfully.

Then the bike pair settles beside your actual process:

**What the customer says → what you find → parts → what you did → test ride.**

A brief context strip identifies your co-op work from 2023 and Hallam Racing membership from October 2025. Your workshop logbook appears as another confirmed working document.

The section explains your process through the documents you use, without padding the page with a separate biography.

**Visitor can click:** the relevant Slow Miles post once its real URL exists, and an evidence-detail disclosure containing the available image or source summary.

**3. Parts — all three projects together**

Approximately one and a quarter screens.

All six cards spread into three paired exhibits:

- **Bike restoration:** inventory, documented findings and writing.
- **Pedal-box mounting bracket:** redesign involvement, reported CAD/simulation reduction, awaiting manufacture and physical testing.
- **Hand-crank charger:** four-person module project, your gear train and housing, and the reported prototype result.

Each project has a short HTML summary, explicit status and a link to its details. Faces remain nearly front-on so images are inspectable while their text is being read.

This is where a recruiter can compare the whole body of work at a glance.

**Visitor can click:** any project’s detail link and any available image to view it larger. Ordinary links and buttons handle everything; dragging is unnecessary.

**4. Work carried out — your contribution**

Approximately one and a quarter screens.

The three pairs align vertically beside their contribution records. Selecting a project brings its pair forward slightly.

This section adds attribution rather than repeating the gallery:

- **Bracket:** what you redesigned, with the limits of the current evidence. Collaborator details remain pending.
- **Charger:** gear train and housing were your parts; the project had four people.
- **Bike:** your restoration and its documented inventory and findings.

A compact skills line includes SolidWorks, MATLAB and some Python. Lathe and mill experience is described as workshop induction, without implying independent machining proficiency.

Project details expand inline, keeping the main scroll short. They hold the project context, your contribution, available evidence and known limitations. Missing information stays out.

**Visitor can click:** each project’s detail disclosure and available evidence images. Opening details does not make someone replay the animation.

**5. Test ride — evidence, limits and contact**

Approximately one and a half screens, in two beats.

The pairs first form a row with explicit written statuses:

- **Bike work:** test rides belong to your confirmed co-op process. The page does not claim a particular completed test ride for the restoration.
- **Charger:** it worked poorly—your reported observation was four minutes of cranking for one percentage point of charge. This is not presented as a controlled efficiency measurement.
- **Bracket:** 18% lighter in CAD/simulation, not manufactured or physically tested at the time of your update.

“Test ride” is the job-card heading. The content distinguishes bike checks, prototype observations and bracket validation.

Finally, the six cards return to one stack. The close answers the opening question by making the boundary between a promising design and a checked result clear.

It then offers a direct placement contact action, CV and project links. The planned November machining is dated and updated only when you confirm what happened.

**Visitor can click:** email, CV download, Slow Miles, each project and back to top.

**Navigation throughout**

A small desktop rail names the five chapters. It shows the current chapter and lets visitors jump directly.

Project links and a contact shortcut are available from the opening. Direct links land at the relevant section without replaying earlier scenes. Browser back and forward retain normal behaviour.

The scroll remains native. Motion happens between reading positions; cards settle while their evidence is being read. There is no scroll snapping, forced dwell, sound or continuous spinning.

**The look**

I’ve chosen **warm workshop paper**.

| Element | Colour |
|---|---|
| Page ground | Warm off-white `#F3EFE6` |
| Card surface | Light paper `#FFFCF4` |
| Text | Charcoal `#242824` |
| Accent | Deep green `#285745` |

The surfaces have fine printed rules, restrained edge shadows and subtle thickness. Photographs and CAD remain the visual focus. Status is always written in words; green does not automatically mean “passed.”

**Source Sans 3** handles reading text and headings. **IBM Plex Mono** handles card fields and small record labels.

Desktop body text is around 18px, with comfortable line lengths. The name has presence without occupying an empty screen. The paper has no fake handwriting, grease stains, signatures or invented measurements.

This material treatment is a design choice, not a claim about your workshop’s appearance.

**On a phone**

The phone version uses the same five chapters in a single column.

Static evidence cards sit in normal document flow by default. Your name, one proof point and project/contact links appear before the first large image. There is no pinned full-screen canvas competing with the text.

Project pairs stack vertically with their relationship labelled. Navigation becomes compact text links. Details expand inline, images can open larger, and every control works by tapping.

Text is approximately 16–18px, controls have comfortable touch areas, and nothing depends on hover or sideways scrolling.

A small optional scene could be considered later for capable devices, but the planned phone experience is complete without it.

**Without 3D or motion**

| Situation | What the visitor receives |
|---|---|
| Reduced motion | Static settled cards; no translation, rotation, parallax or animated scrolling |
| No WebGL | HTML evidence cards and approved images, with the same pairings and status labels |
| No JavaScript | All five chapters, normal anchor links, native detail disclosures, images, contact and CV |
| Missing or uncleared images | Factual text records in the same card layout |

All essential text lives in ordinary HTML. The canvas holds no exclusive evidence, navigation or contact information.

A screen reader follows the five chapters in order. The decorative canvas is excluded from its reading path; meaningful images receive useful descriptions.

**Everything else the site needs**

“Include” below means a future implementation. This task remains planning only.

| Requirement | Decision |
|---|---|
| Navigation | Include chapter anchors, direct project links, contact shortcut, skip link and visible keyboard focus |
| Complete project coverage | Include bike, bracket and charger; place co-op and Hallam context in Findings |
| Project detail | Include substantive inline details initially; separate case-study pages later when fuller evidence warrants them |
| Contact | Include a real public email link; no contact form initially |
| CV | Include an accessible PDF with current dates, qualified bracket claims and no guessed repair count or misleading team achievement |
| Slow Miles | Keep separate and link to it; do not fabricate full posts from supplied summaries |
| Testimonials | Omit, as you requested |
| Languages | English initially |
| Search metadata | Factual page title, description and canonical address |
| Shared-link preview | Job-card composition using cleared images or typography |
| Site icon | Simple card-outline favicon |
| Missing-page handling | A useful 404 linking home, projects and contact |
| Accessibility | Semantic headings, keyboard access, contrast checks, image descriptions, zoom/reflow and motion preferences |
| Privacy | No tracking planned; document actual hosting/service data handling before publication |
| Legal notice | Establish applicable requirements before publication without guessing your jurisdiction or address |
| Hosting and domain | Choose in a later deployment task; no purchase or deployment now |
| Chat | Omit |
| Maintenance | Keep project contributions and statuses editable; explicitly update manufacturing and testing claims |

**Performance and future verification**

The text and opening evidence load before the optional scene. The scene uses six simple card shapes, restrained lighting and compressed images. Rendering pauses when offscreen or the tab is hidden.

Future checks should establish that:

- A recruiter can identify you, inspect evidence and reach you without scrolling or waiting for 3D.
- The main story fits a two-minute review.
- Phone, keyboard, reduced-motion and no-JavaScript paths contain the same information.
- Contact links, CV dates, attribution and asset permissions are correct.
- Mobile performance meets sensible targets: LCP within 2.5 seconds, CLS at or below 0.1, and INP within 200ms. These are targets, not measured results.

I chose the concept, colours, typography, contact action, separate-blog arrangement and inline project structure using your authorization. Unconfirmed facts remain explicit. Final captions and website code are later work; this completes the planning-only handover.
